newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway Christiania, Storebrand seek merger.
newsitem.headline: Norway Christiania, Storebrand seek merger.

text.p: Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA and Storebrand ASA, Norway's leading insurer, announced plans to merge Wednesday to form the largest financial group in Norway and the sixth biggest in the Nordic region.
The new company, to be called Christiania Group, would be the second largest company on the Oslo Stock exchange after industrial giant Norsk Hydro ASA.
"The merger is the next logical step in the development of the two groups, which have both followed a strategy of providing a broad range of financial services," a joint statement said.

"The merged group will be able to play a more active role in a developing Nordic market and be better positioned for profitable growth than if each of the two groups were to remain separate," it said.

Each set of shareholders will hold 50 percent of the combined company. The agreed exchange ratio was based on market values with two ordinary shares in Christiania Bank equivalent to one ordinary Storebrand share.
The companies said they hoped to complete the deal by year end following government approval.

"The merger is very exciting in terms of benefits both on the costs and revenues side," insurance analyst Nils Ringdal at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson in London said. "We see benefits of between 15 (percent) and 25 percent in terms of increased pre-tax profits in a few years, say in 2000 or 2001."

The companies said the Christiania Bank and Storebrand brands would be retained and the principal elements of the two groups' operating structures -- banking, non-life insurance, life insurance/pensions and asset management -- would continue.

The merged Christiania will have a combined market share of 32 percent in the life insurance sector, 5 percentage points higher than Storebrand's current position, when Christiania Bank insurance division Norske Liv's market share is included.

In non-life insurance, the new group will have 39 percent of the market, while it will hold a market share of about 12 percent in traditional banking products, equal to Chrisitiania Bank's current position.

Aage Korsvold, chief executive at Storebrand and proposed CEO of the Christiania, said the company may look to expand in the Nordic market althought there were no concrete plans on an all-Nordic basis or at home.
Norway's overcrowded banking sector has been undergoing consolidation since the late 1980s and further mergers had been expected in the battle for market share amid slimmer margins.
